problem: The Dittert conjecture concerning the maximum achieved by a particular function of matrices with real, nonnegative entries satisfying a summation condition
missing_details: Definition of the domain: A is an n×n matrix with nonnegative real entries and total sum of entries equal to n
Precise definition of the function φ(A) in terms of row sums, column sums, and the permanent
Specification of the candidate maximizer A=(1/n)J_n and definition of J_n
refined_question: Let n be a positive integer and let A=[a_{ij}] be an n×n matrix with real nonnegative entries satisfying ∑_{i=1}^n ∑_{j=1}^n a_{ij}=n. Define the permanent of A by per(A)=∑_{σ∈S_n}∏_{i=1}^n a_{i,σ(i)}, and define φ(A)=∏_{i=1}^n(∑_{j=1}^n a_{ij})+∏_{j=1}^n(∑_{i=1}^n a_{ij})−per(A). Does φ(A) attain its maximum value uniquely when A=(1/n)J_n, where J_n denotes the n×n matrix with all entries equal to 1?
justification: The problem name indicates that one seeks the maximum of a certain function on nonnegative matrices with a summation constraint but does not specify the exact function (φ), its components (row sums, column sums, permanent), the domain constraints (total sum equals n), or the conjectured maximizer (J_n scaled by 1/n). These details are essential for a stand-alone statement of the conjecture.
